svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: The agentic enterprise target-state architecture on one page
svg.desc: Fourteen enterprise layers grouped into seven planes. Each layer shows its control point and three key mechanisms. Ten cross-cutting concerns run as columns across every layer, marked where each layer owns or enforces them. Four deterministic zones sit underneath as boundaries that no model decision crosses.
svg.text: The agentic enterprise, on one page
Fourteen layers of estate. Seven planes of agent system across them. Ten concerns through every layer. Four boundaries no model decision crosses.
Products named for orientation as of August 2026. Representative, not exhaustive,
and not endorsements. Vendor capability claims are vendor-published.
Enforcement lives in the control plane, never in the execution plane. An instruction in a prompt is a preference; the same rule at a gateway is a control.
The evidence plane is fed by collection the agent cannot influence. Anything an agent reports about itself is testimony, not evidence.
Harness caps and eval-gated registry promotion
One gateway is the single enforcement point
Entitlement stays in the record system
NREL eGridGPT (reference architecture, not a product)
Information path only; operator holds authority
Fail-close ACL pre-filter inside the query
Provenance at parse time; erasure cascades
Deterministic PDP on every consequential action
Registry, evidence tier, kill switch before autonomy
Counterexample-gated promotion with a demotion path
Collection outside the agent; hard budget caps
Access identity default; presence by exception
Separate edge on the shared control plane
Burst-rate oversight capacity, never a daily average
Concerns are properties, not products. These are the categories that carry them; the enforcement point still sits where the matrix above says it does.
Entra Agent ID, Okta for AI Agents, CyberArk, SailPoint, SPIFFE/WIMSE
Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, LangSmith, Braintrust, Langfuse
Microsoft Purview, OneTrust, Credo AI, IBM watsonx.governance
Glean, Azure AI Search ACLs, Amazon Q, dbt Semantic Layer, Cube
Disclosure and content-marking tooling; thin market, mostly platform features
AWS European Sovereign Cloud, Google Distributed Cloud, sovereign regions
OneTrust, Purview, erasure and DSAR tooling reaching derived artifacts
ServiceNow AI Control Tower; guardrail products, advisory only
LiteLLM budgets, Agent 365 billing policies, FOCUS 1.3, Tokenomics
Temporal, Restate, DBOS, Inngest; degraded-mode design is yours
Four deterministic zones. Models may inform, never decide.
These hold under every layer above. Three of the four already run machine-learning signals inside them; the decision rule stays deterministic.
Rule over verified identity; risk scores advise
Scoped, revocable mandates; fraud models advise
Standards exclude ML from the function itself
Owns the concern: defines the requirement and holds accountability
Enforces it: where a violation is actually stopped
Inherits it: must carry the property through without weakening it
Inheritance is where most defects live, because it fails silently.
